title: Be mindful of Allah
hook: be mindful of Allah and He will protect you, the pens have been lifted and the pages dried (Nawawi 19, Ibn Abbas)
tomorrow: the hadith says this line came from earlier prophets. what is it?

segments.voice: Yesterday: follow a bad deed with a good, because the good erases it, a comma and not a full stop. Today's words were spoken to a boy, and they're about waiting.

Waiting is its own job. A test result, an offer, an answer from someone who matters. You refresh the page. You ask a friend whether it'll be fine, then another friend. Each yes helps for about ten minutes. Then the loop starts again. One day a boy, Abdullah ibn Abbas, was behind the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the Prophet turned and said: young man, I'll teach you some words. They land right in the middle of a refresh loop.
screen: `REFRESH. ASK. REFRESH.` → `TEN MINUTES OF CALM.` → `YOUNG MAN, I'LL TEACH YOU SOME WORDS.`

segments.voice: From Sunan al-Tirmidhi, in paraphrase: be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you'll find Him in front of you. When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek it from Allah. If the whole community gathered to help you, they could help only with what Allah had already written for you. If they gathered to harm you, they could harm only with what was already written. The pens have been lifted, and the pages have dried. Mindful here is ihfaz: keep, guard, look after. Keep Allah's limits and His rights, and He keeps you. That's the exchange, and it runs both ways. And notice where Allah is found: in front of you. Not behind, checking up. Ahead, already there when you arrive. For a week of waiting, look at the middle. The hadith doesn't forbid talking it through with a friend. It turns the deepest asking, the three-in-the-morning kind, toward one place. The friends can't settle it. The refresh button can't. The pages have dried. Some hear that as heavy. Many readers hear it as rest: whatever the crowd does, it can't add to what's written or take it away. Do your part, keep His limits, and put the asking where the hadith puts it. He will protect you.
screen: `KEEP ALLAH; HE KEEPS YOU.` · `ASK HIM; SEEK HIS HELP.` · `THE CROWD CAN'T REWRITE IT.` · `THE PAGES HAVE DRIED.` · then, large: `HE WILL PROTECT YOU.`

segments.voice: If you pray, ask Allah for one thing in your own words, quietly and out loud, and then let the sit hold it instead of your phone. If not, say the thing you're waiting on out loud once, plainly, and let the quiet carry it for a while. No need to fill the silence afterward.
Be mindful of Allah: ihfaz Allah, keep Him, guard His limits, wherever you are. The promise follows straight after: He will protect you.
Carry this: he will protect you, and the dried pages can be a place to rest. Hadith nineteen, kept.

screen: `DAY 1447 COUNTS.` → `THE FORTY · 19 OF 42.` → `TOMORROW: THE HADITH SAYS THIS LINE CAME FROM EARLIER PROPHETS. WHAT IS IT?`

howItsDone: Many Muslims memorize this hadith in Arabic, and some recite its lines in hard seasons; it often frames du'a, asking Allah directly, alongside ordinary effort.

original.note: Arabic: be mindful of Allah; literally keep or guard Allah: His limits and His rights.

trapdoor: what you thought: a promise that life will go your way.
what it means: keep Allah's limits and you'll find Him in front of you; the deepest asking goes to Him, and no crowd can rewrite what's written.
what a scholar hears: Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2516 (Ibn Abbas); a longer version in Musnad Ahmad adds more lines, including on patience and relief.

chat.says: early decision drops thursday. i've asked 5 people if i'll get in. dadi says 'ask the right One.'
options: she means the hadith: ask Allah, do your part, and let the pages rest.
ask a sixth person; asking around is how you get the real odds.
stop hoping at all; it's already written, so nothing you do matters.
chat.meaning: The hadith turns the deepest asking toward Allah; 'already written' is a rest after doing your part, not a reason to quit.

Abdullah ibn Abbas.meaning: the Prophet's young cousin, later a great scholar

Sunan al-Tirmidhi.meaning: a hadith collection compiled by al-Tirmidhi

hadith.meaning: a report of what the Prophet said or did
